office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent April Berg, chair of the House Finance Committee, faces first-time Republican candidate Tonya Stadlman, a 30-year housing-industry manager. Berg helped lead the 2026 tax on income over $1 million; Stadlman runs on lower taxes, auditing spending, permitting reform and restoring parental rights.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2021 and House Finance Committee chair, a former Everett and Edmonds school board director who says she helped lead the 2026 Millionaires Tax.
highlights: Says she helped lead the Millionaires Tax, 'the first step in addressing our regressive tax structure' [S3][S5]
Platform supports the Housing Trust Fund, permanent supportive housing and universal childcare [S2]
Supports clean fuel standards and science-based climate action [S2]
Voted for EHB 1217 (2025 rent-increase limits) and ESHB 1296 (2025 parents' rights amendments) [S11][S12]

taxes.basis: Finance chair who voted for ESSB 6346 and says she helped lead it as a fix for a regressive tax code in which 'the wealthiest few paid far less than their fair share'.

spending.basis: Platform calls for universal childcare, more early-learning and school funding and housing investment; pamphlet says 'more needs to be done' after current investments.

housing.basis: Platform supports the Housing Trust Fund, permanent supportive housing and fewer barriers for shelters; voted for the 2025 rent and fee increase limits.

climate.basis: Platform supports clean fuel standards and science-based climate action; endorsed by Washington Conservation Action.

experience.basis: Incumbent since 2021 and Finance Committee chair, with prior school-board service; opponent has never held office.

social.basis: Lists a Planned Parenthood endorsement and is endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no statement of her own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 list of parent and guardian rights; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: First-time Republican candidate with 30 years managing affordable and conventional housing, running on a 'Six to Fix' platform of lower taxes, audits, permitting reform, public safety and parental rights.
highlights: Would cut household costs 'starting with the gas tax' and 'audit where the money is going' before new revenue [S2]
Says 'you cannot make housing more affordable by making housing more expensive to build' [S2]
Safety plan pairs consequences for repeat offenders with treatment and recovery [S2]
Pledges to 'restore and protect parental rights' and parents' access to information about their children's education [S2]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet pledges 'lower taxes'; platform would cut the gas tax first, audit before asking for revenue and examine B&O reform.

spending.basis: Platform standard 'Audit Before Ask'; says more spending or programs do not solve problems and calls for auditing programs and measuring outcomes.

housing.basis: Would reduce barriers, speed permitting and encourage starter homes, arguing that regulation makes housing more expensive.

safety.basis: Supports law enforcement and consequences for repeat offenders, cites low police staffing, and adds treatment and recovery for addiction-driven crime.

climate.basis: Would start household cost relief with the gas tax; no other energy or climate positions.

experience.basis: Has not held public office; running against the Finance Committee chair.

parental-rights.basis: Pledges to 'restore and protect parental rights and ensure parents have access to important information about their children's education and well-being'.
